gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Battle Born's heated LiFePO4 runs its heater from the battery's own stored energy, and that the heater does nothing until the heat-enable post is wired to the positive terminal. In a series bank, those posts are chained together and fed from the highest-voltage positive terminal. Redodo's heater works the other way: it only runs when a charger is connected and cuts in at 32°F.
standout_why: I compared against ChatGPT's answer and the one page it cited, Power Queen's self-heating product page. The answer only says some heaters run on incoming charge current and gives Power Queen's 10 A minimum. It never mentions a heater powered by the battery itself, and it never says a heater can need extra wiring to work at all. I tried to open the Power Queen, SOK, Vatrer, Battle Born and Renogy product pages, but each one returned a certificate error, 404, 403 or 429. So I could not confirm whether the uncited Battle Born product pages (results 6–9) mention the heat-enable jumper. That gap is why I scored this 2, not 3.
decides: This splits the candidates into two kinds of heater. Charger-powered heaters (Redodo per its own store listing; SOK per a search summary I could not open) cannot warm a battery sitting in storage or on a weak winter panel, because the charger is what runs the heater. Battle Born warms from its own charge, so it suits batteries left unattended in the cold, but only if the installer adds the heat-enable jumper, or a switch to stop the heater draining the battery in storage. For a shopper charging from a big shore charger or DC-DC charger, Redodo at $251.99 is still the budget pick. For a shopper with small solar or a parked RV, a self-powered heater like Battle Born's is the safer match.

findings.label: Heater power source
findings.value: The battery's own internal power, not a charger
findings.source_title: How to Wire Integrated Battery Heating and Heat Enable | The Battle Born Educational Series
findings.note: Maker's own article: 'Because the heating system uses internal battery power, it may take time...'

findings.label: Wiring needed before the heater works
findings.value: A jumper from the positive terminal to the heat-enable post; an inline switch is optional
findings.source_title: How to Wire Integrated Battery Heating and Heat Enable | The Battle Born Educational Series
findings.note: Maker's own wording: 'The heating system will not activate unless the heat-enable circuit is connected.' The optional switch lets you turn heating off so it doesn't drain the battery in storage.

findings.label: Heat-enable wiring for a multi-battery bank
findings.value: Chain the heat-enable posts together and take the feed from the highest-voltage positive terminal in the system (12, 24 or 48 V)
findings.source_title: How to Wire Integrated Battery Heating and Heat Enable | The Battle Born Educational Series
findings.note: Maker's own wording: 'Always enable heating from the highest voltage point in the system.'

findings.label: Heater on/off temperatures, charge limit and warm-up time
findings.value: Heater turns on below about 35°F and off around 45°F; charging allowed above about 25°F; about 2–4 h to warm up from freezing
findings.source_title: How to Wire Integrated Battery Heating and Heat Enable | The Battle Born Educational Series
findings.note: Same maker article. The page shows the 'Heated' icon on these models: 100Ah 12V, 100Ah 12V GC2, 270Ah 12V GC3, 50Ah 24V and 75Ah 12V Group 24.

findings.label: Heater on/off temperatures and charge/discharge cutoffs
findings.value: Heater turns on below 32°F (0°C) and stops at 41°F (5°C), then charging resumes; charging blocked below 32°F; discharge stops below -4°F; 100 W dual heating pads
findings.source_title: Redodo 12V 100Ah Self-Heating Lithium Battery | For RV, Boats, and Solar Home Systems
findings.note: Taken from the maker's US Shopify store data via storecheck.py search; the description text it returned was cut short.

findings.label: Maximum system size
findings.value: 51.2 V 400 Ah, 20.48 kWh (4 in series × 4 in parallel)
findings.source_title: Redodo 12V 100Ah Self-Heating Lithium Battery | For RV, Boats, and Solar Home Systems
findings.note: The maker says 'Max. 20.48kWh System Expansion... 51.2V 400Ah'. 51.2 V = 4 × 12.8 V in series, and 400 Ah = 4 × 100 Ah in parallel, so 16 batteries × 1.28 kWh = 20.48 kWh.
